intro: Browse normal and emergency training procedures. Each procedure opens as a focused reference view with a clear return path.
footerNote: H125 / AS350 B3 (2B1) training reference. For training use only. Always cross-check with the latest approved RFM.

procedures.title: BEFORE START / PREFLIGHT AND PRE-START CHECKS

right: On board and current. Verify all required documents and check that applicable revisions are incorporated.
Confirm that all corrective maintenance necessary for flightworthiness is completed (Section 4.2).
Perform preflight inspection per RFM Section 4.2, including MGB and TGB oil levels, rotor blades, controls, cowls and leaks. If parked > 2 days or in case of doubt, open cowls.
Check weight, CG and loading are within Section 2 limitations; record any exceedance as required by Section 4.1.
Before the first flight of the day and if OAT is at or above 0 °C, bleed the fuel tank at the drain point and confirm no leakage at the bleed valve.
Secure baggage and cabin freight in accordance with cabin loading instructions and placards.
Check ELT in
position and configure radios, transponder and navigation equipment as required.
Select [BAT/EPU] or external power as applicable. Verify DC voltages within limits.
Rotor brake released, lever fully forward before engine start (Section 4.3).
Forward, with guard in place. Confirm fuel system configured for start, fuel quantity sufficient and approved fuel per Section 2.5.
IDLE position for prestart checks.
UP position. Verify engine control and VEMD powered.
OFF, then select START according to RFM procedure, monitoring Ng, t4 and oil pressure.
Monitor t4 and Ng during start; abort in case of abnormal rise or failure to accelerate as per limitations and emergency procedures.
Allow engine to stabilize in ground idle. Check VEMD indications and absence of abnormal warnings.
Complete remaining checks and progress to rotor engagement according to Section 4.3.
At ground idle and then flight condition, verify Ng, Nf/NR, Tq and t4 within normal operating ranges.
Check full and free movement in all axes, friction adjusted as required, no abnormal forces or stops.
No red warnings; only expected advisories on CWP and VEMD before lift-off.
Establish a stable hover in HIGE at around 5 ft (1.5 m). Check attitude, power required and control response.

In HIGE at about 5 ft (1.5 m) before initiating forward flight, raise collective slightly to confirm that Ng can increase by at least 1 % without exceeding the maximum transient rating, and that the torque required is compatible with the take-off/landing environment and weight (Section 5.1).
Complete remaining checklist items (instruments, doors, harnesses, lights) prior to forward flight.
From a stabilized hover or low-speed run, smoothly accelerate while maintaining NR within limits.

Accelerate towards Vy for best rate of climb. As a guide, Vy is approximately 65 kt IAS at sea level and decreases by about 1 kt for each 1000 ft of pressure altitude (≈ 120 km/h minus 2 km/h per 300 m).

At high internal gross weight, use HIGE power to accelerate along the take-off path until IAS reaches about 40 kt, then begin the climb so as to clear roughly 20 ft (6 m) at around 50 kt (93 km/h), in line with the height–velocity diagram guidance (SUP.28).
Maintain power within MCP or applicable take-off limits; monitor Tq and t4 margins.
Establish climb at Vy or as required by obstacle and terrain; monitor Hp and temperature limits.
Complete after take-off checklist when safely established in climb.

procedures.title: CLIMB
procedures.rfmReference: AS350 B3 2B1 RFM Section 4.5 §1 and Section 5.1

right: Above about 100 ft (30 m) AGL, establish a stable climb attitude with NR in the normal range and power within the recommended continuous or take-off ratings.

For maximum climb performance, use Vy. As a guide, Vy ≈ 65 kt IAS at sea level, reducing by about 1 kt per 1000 ft of pressure altitude (≈ 120 km/h minus 2 km/h per 300 m). Adjust as required for obstacles and ATC.
Monitor Tq and t4, keeping margins to transient and maximum limits. Adjust collective to keep a steady climb rate and avoid over-torque or over-temperature.
Approaching cruise altitude, smoothly reduce collective while adjusting cyclic to accelerate or decelerate to desired cruise speed, avoiding abrupt attitude changes.
Complete any after-climb checklist items when stabilized in cruise (pressurization, engine instruments, fuel).

procedures.title: CRUISE FLIGHT AND MANEUVERS
procedures.rfmReference: AS350 B3 2B1 RFM Section 4.5 §2 and Section 5.1

right: Establish cruise at a speed and torque setting compatible with fuel planning and limitations; use Section 5.1 tables as a reference.
Over noise-sensitive areas, the complementary manual recommends IAS ≈ 110 kt (204 km/h) for OAT +25 °C, adjusted slightly with temperature, and at least 1000 ft AGL where possible.
Trim the helicopter for hands-light flight where possible to reduce pilot workload and improve stability.
Perform turns and basic maneuvers with smooth, coordinated control inputs, respecting bank angle, load factor and speed limitations given in Sections 2 and 4.5.
Continuously monitor engine/vehicle instruments, fuel balance, and navigation; adjust power and attitude to maintain stable flight.
Plan top-of-descent and brief the approach, taking into account terrain, airspace and weather.

procedures.title: DESCENT AND APPROACH
procedures.rfmReference: AS350 B3 2B1 RFM Section 4.5 §3 and Section 5.1

right: Reduce collective smoothly to start descent, keeping NR within normal range and avoiding abrupt power changes.

Adjust cyclic and collective to achieve a stabilized descent profile. For noise-sensitive helipads, use about 60 kt (111 km/h) with a rate of descent close to 1000 ft/min; for approaches near sensitive areas but landing elsewhere, use Vy with around 500 ft/min as a reference.
Monitor Tq, t4, Ng and NR; avoid prolonged low-power descents outside of the conditions allowed by the RFM, and respect all limitations.

Transition from en-route descent to the final approach by aligning with the landing site, confirming wind and obstacles and configuring lights and avionics as required. Plan to be around 100 ft (30 m) AGL when reducing towards a HIGE hover at roughly 5 ft (1.5 m).
Complete approach/landing checks before entering low-level or confined-area segments of the approach.
Assess landing site, slope and wind; ensure slope and surface are within limitations (Section 2.3).

Plan a stabilized approach, managing airspeed and rate of descent within normal envelopes. As a guide, begin the approach around Vy (see climb section) and, in noise-sensitive areas, consider 60 kt (111 km/h) with a rate of descent close to 1000 ft/min or Vy with about 500 ft/min when approaching a helipad near sensitive areas.
Transition to hover as needed; maintain safe clearance and cross-check instruments and power.

Lower collective smoothly to touch down, maintaining attitude and heading with cyclic and pedals. For any planned running landing in normal operations, keep ground speed well below the 40 kt (74 km/h) running landing limitation (Section 2.3).
Stabilize helicopter on ground, then complete post-landing checks and prepare for shutdown as applicable.

procedures.title: ENGINE SHUTDOWN AND SECURING THE HELICOPTER

right: At ground idle, verify engine and vehicle parameters within limits and note any abnormal indications.
Apply normal shutdown procedure from the RFM, including twist grip to IDLE then OFF as prescribed.

Allow rotor to decelerate per limitations. If rotor brake is used, apply it below approximately 170 rpm in high wind conditions or below 140 rpm in normal conditions, as specified in Section 4.6. In high-wind operations, starting and stopping the rotor has been demonstrated up to about 40 kt (74 km/h) from any direction and 50 kt (93 km/h) headwind; for winds above roughly 40 kt, park the helicopter into wind and tie it down per Section 4.8.
Switch off unnecessary consumers, then [GEN], [BAT/EPU] or external power according to shutdown sequence.
Install control locks or collective friction as required, fit covers and blade tie-downs per Section 4.2 guidance.
Stabilized level flight at a power rating close to MCP with Hp ≤ 12000 ft and heating/demisting OFF.
Select the ENGINE POWER CHECK page on the VEMD and perform the check according to Section 5.1.
Check that TRQ MARGIN is positive and T4 MARGIN is negative with
displayed; engine health check is satisfactory in this case.
If VEMD result is not clearly satisfactory, record Tq, Ng, NR, Hp, OAT and t4 and apply the manual ENGINE POWER CHECK and t4 CHECK charts per RFM.

When necessary, compute corrected t4 margin using the Hp/OAT correction table. This correction only applies when the initial T4 margin is ≥ +35 °C; if the corrected margin is negative the result is acceptable, whereas a T4 margin greater than +35 °C means the engine condition is unsatisfactory.

If both VEMD screens fail, the maximum authorized power is the power required to maintain level flight while following the law IAS = 100 kt at 0 Hp minus 2 kt per 1000 ft (or 185 km/h minus 4 km/h per 300 m), as described in Section 3.5.
If margins are unsatisfactory, treat as an engine performance issue and follow maintenance/operational guidance.

procedures.title: CRANKING PROCEDURE
procedures.rfmReference: AS350 B3 2B1 RFM – Normal revision 6 / related procedure

right: Use cranking only for the purposes and under the conditions specified in the RFM (e.g. maintenance, engine drying).
Set fuel system, twist grip and engine controls to the positions specified for cranking (no fuel to combustion).
Engage starter according to the RFM, monitoring Ng and respecting starter duty cycle limitations.
Monitor t4, oil pressure and electrical parameters; abort if any abnormal indication occurs.
Allow starter to cool according to limitations before any subsequent start or cranking cycle.

procedures.title: ENGINE FLAME-OUT & AUTOROTATION
procedures.subtitle: Cruise, over water, hover IGE, hover OGE, in-flight relighting

right: Collective — REDUCE to maintain NR in the normal operating range.
IAS — Vy.

steps.left: Cruise — 3–4 (after loss of tail rotor thrust)
right: Twist grip IDLE; maneuver into the wind on final approach.
Cyclic — FLARE.
Collective — GRADUALLY INCREASE to reduce rate of descent and forward speed.
Cyclic FORWARD for a slightly nose-up landing attitude (below 10°).
Pedals — ADJUST to cancel any sideslip tendency.
Collective — INCREASE to cushion touchdown.
Cyclic, collective, pedals — ADJUST to control the ground run.
Collective full low pitch; apply the rotor brake below 170 rotor rpm.

Same procedure except items 10–12: head equally between wind and wave direction on final, ditch with minimum forward speed (IAS below 30 kt / 56 km/h) and minimum rate of descent. After touchdown: collective MAINTAIN, doors jettison handles PULL-UP, rotor brake APPLY; abandon once the rotor has stopped.
Maintain collective; control yaw with the pedals; increase collective as needed to cushion touchdown.
A safe autorotative landing cannot be ensured after a failure in HOGE below the top point of the HV diagram or in a confined area.
Collective full low pitch. When NR stops decreasing, cyclic forward to gain airspeed according to the available height, then apply the autorotation procedure.
Engine starting selector — OFF.
[FUEL P] / [FUEL PUMP] — ON.
Engine starting selector — ON. The relighting sequence then runs automatically as soon as Ng is below 17 %.
[FUEL P] / [FUEL PUMP] — OFF. At least 1000 ft (300 m) are needed to complete the relighting procedure after a flame-out.
Heating and demisting — OFF. If the smoke clears, continue depending on atmospheric conditions.
[MASTER SW] or [EMER SW] — SHUT OFF; [EXT PWR BATT] or [BAT/EPU] — OFF; [DCT BAT] (if fitted) — OFF.
[GEN] or [GENE] — OFF; [AVIONIC] (if fitted) — OFF; ventilate the cabin.

All consumers OFF; then [MASTER SW]/[EMER SW] ON, [DCT BAT] ON, [EXT PWR BATT]/[BAT/EPU] ON (check DC parameters), [GEN]/[GENE] ON (check DC parameters). Continue flight depending on atmospheric conditions.
LAND AS SOON AS POSSIBLE. If DC parameters are not correct: [GEN]/[GENE] OFF and apply case A of the GENE DC generator off-line procedure.
[AVIONIC] ON, then minimum required consumers ON one by one; if smoke returns, switch that system off for the rest of the flight. LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE or continue depending on conditions.
With [MASTER SW]/[EMER SW] actuated, or battery and generator off line, the VEMD goes off: apply the failure-of-both-screens procedure (Section 3.5 §1).

Corresponding system OFF; ventilate the cabin; continue depending on the failed system. After DC has been switched off and on in flight, GOV stays lit until the next normal full engine shutdown and battery-off on the ground.

procedures.title: ENGINE FIRE, GOVERNOR & FADEC FAILURES
procedures.subtitle: Fire in engine bay, governor failure, minor FADEC failure, oil pressure, chip detection

right: Engine starting selector OFF; emergency fuel shut-off handle AFT; [FUEL P]/[FUEL PUMP] OFF; [CRANK] press 10 s; rotor brake APPLY (≤ 170 rpm); [MASTER SW]/[EMER SW] OFF; evacuate and fight the fire from outside.
LAND IMMEDIATELY with a no-hover powered landing; once on the ground apply the start-up sequence.

LAND IMMEDIATELY: collective LOWER, IAS Vy, autorotation procedure APPLY, emergency fuel shut-off handle AFT, [FUEL P] CHECK OFF, engine starting selector OFF. After landing: rotor brake APPLY (≤ 170 rpm), [MASTER SW]/[EMER SW] OFF, evacuate and fight the fire from outside.

Emergency mode engages automatically and GOV lights. Check flight parameters. Avoid abrupt collective changes. Maintain Ng above 80 % below 20 000 ft (6096 m), above 85 % at or above 20 000 ft. LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE.

steps.left: Major governor failure — approach and landing
right: Make a powered approach and avoid a steep angle. After touchdown lower the collective slowly to low pitch and select the engine starting selector OFF. The VEHICLE page shows FF and END; Ng and torque can also be lost on the VEMD.
Engine starting selector OFF immediately.
Governing degraded: avoid abrupt power changes, keep IAS below VNE power off, LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE. On the ground do not start the engine.
Governor redundancy failure with no impact on governing: abort a start-up (see the Maintenance Manual), or cancel autorotation training and return to base.

steps.left: Engine oil pressure at or below 1.1 bar (16 psi)
right: Check the gauge. LOW or NIL: LAND IMMEDIATELY — autorotation procedure, shut down the engine time permitting. NORMAL (CWP light test completed): LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE.

steps.left: Twist grip out of FLIGHT position
right: Turn the twist grip to FLIGHT. Continue flight.

steps.left: Metal particles in engine oil circuit
right: Reduce power; LAND AS SOON AS POSSIBLE with a low-power approach and be ready for a loss of engine power. Takeoff is prohibited until the engine manufacturer's checks are complete.

procedures.title: TRANSMISSION & HYDRAULIC FAILURES
procedures.subtitle: MGB oil pressure and temperature, chip detection, hydraulic pressure loss

steps.left: MGB low oil pressure (below 1 bar / 14.5 psi)
right: Reduce power; LAND AS SOON AS POSSIBLE. If a safe landing is not possible, continue to the nearest suitable site at minimum power speed (Vy). 55 min of simulated flight at low power has been shown in bench tests.
Set IAS to Vy, monitor the CWP; land as soon as practicable — or as soon as possible depending on the trend.

steps.left: Metal particles in MGB oil circuit
right: Reduce power and monitor; LAND AS SOON AS POSSIBLE.

steps.left: Metal particles in TGB oil circuit
right: Avoid prolonged hovering; continue flight.
Do not use [HYD TEST] or [ACCU TST]: it depressurizes the yaw load compensator and gives heavy pedal loads.

steps.left: Hydraulic failure — HIGE, takeoff, final (landing within 30 s possible)
right: Land normally, collective LOCK, twist grip IDLE, apply shutdown.
Bank below 30°, avoid abrupt maneuvers, smoothly set IAS 40–60 KIAS (74–111 km/h), then hydraulic cut-off switch OFF. Do not let the twist grip leave FLIGHT as loads rise. LAND AS SOON AS POSSIBLE.

No hover or low-speed maneuvers. Over a clear flat area keep 40–60 KIAS, flat approach into wind, slow no-hover running landing at about 10 kt groundspeed (18.5 km/h). After landing collective LOCK, twist grip IDLE, shutdown.

procedures.title: ELECTRICAL & FUEL ALARMS
procedures.subtitle: Battery, generator, AC/inverter, fuel quantity, pressure and filter, miscellaneous alarms

right: [EXT PWR BATT]/[BAT/EPU] OFF, check U bus voltage. If above Umax: battery ON, [GEN]/[GENE] OFF, unnecessary equipment OFF; land as soon as practicable.
Check [BAT/EPU] ON and the voltage on the VEMD; if not resolved land as soon as practicable, otherwise continue.

Check U bus on the VEMD and [GENE] ON; check the GENE RESET breaker is not popped (30 α panel) and press [GENE RESET]. Case A/B: unnecessary equipment OFF, monitor U bus, land as soon as practicable, or continue if it recovers.
The VEMD goes out and NR/Nf indication is lost: apply the failure-of-both-screens procedure, avoid autorotation, shallow approach with a cautious landing.
Check [INV] ON; if off, all AC consumers are lost — select ON. The AFCS disengages: hands on the controls. Continue flight.
LAND AS SOON AS POSSIBLE; about 15 minutes of flight remain at MCP. Avoid large attitude changes that could cause a flame-out.
Reduce power, [FUEL P]/[FUEL PUMP] ON, land as soon as possible with a low-power approach; be prepared for a flame-out.

Reduce power and establish flight at reduced power; land as soon as practicable — or as soon as possible; monitor Ng on the VEMD. If Ng oscillations occur, LAND IMMEDIATELY and apply the autorotation procedure. Bypass opening drives contamination into the fuel lines and governor.
Check [PITOT] ON; if it was ON, monitor the airspeed indicator; otherwise switch ON. Continue flight.
Check [HORN] ON; switch ON if off. Continue flight.
Reduce to 70 kt (130 km/h); land as soon as practicable with a descent and approach at a low rate of descent.

procedures.title: VEMD SCREEN, NR/Nf & PARAMETER FAILURES
procedures.subtitle: VEMD screen failures, caution messages, abnormal NR/Nf, engine and electrical parameters

right: Failed screen OFF; read the other via [SCROLL] on the VEMD or the collective. If the top screen fails, the 3-parameter engine page moves to the lower screen with torque and ΔNg off line — only t4 and digital Ng remain.
Maximum authorized power is what is needed for level flight at IAS = 100 kt at 0 Hp minus 2 kt per 1000 ft (185 km/h minus 4 km/h per 300 m). LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE with a no-hover landing.

When a parameter is off line its value disappears and its scale turns yellow. Messages are self-explanatory; with no CWP light lit no other action is needed. OVERLIMIT DETECTED stays until 40 % Ng at the next start; check the recorded data after flight.
Maintain collective with torque above 10 % (NR is then read from the Nf pointer); land as soon as practicable.
Check NR in the normal range with torque above 0; continue flight. The EBCAU may not be available.
Set 80 kt (148 km/h). If the temperature decreases, land as soon as practicable; if not, check oil cooler fan operation and land as soon as possible.

steps.left: Low engine oil pressure (CWP ENG P)
right: If confirmed, LAND IMMEDIATELY — autorotation procedure, shut down the engine time permitting; otherwise land as soon as practicable.

steps.left: Loss of Ng, torque or t4
right: The FLI is replaced by 3-data symbology. Ng failure: comply with maximum torque and a t4 limit of 810 °C (the starting limits). Torquemeter failure: comply with the Ng table. Ng and torque lost (GOV): t4 and numeric Ng valid, t4 limit 810 °C. t4 failure: comply with Ng and torque, heating and demisting OFF, no ground start. Land as soon as practicable.
[GEN]/[GENE] OFF, monitor the CWP, apply GENE case A; land as soon as practicable. Between 29.0 V and 31.5 V: monitor U/BUS, continue flight.
Apply the GENE procedure and check U/BUS above 26.0 V — continue if so, otherwise apply case A and land as soon as practicable. The cause is probably a generator defect that does not light GENE.

steps.left: Generator current over limit (red underline flashing)
right: Switch off unnecessary equipment; continue flight. A high generator current after a battery start is normal while the battery recharges.

procedures.title: FLIGHT CONTROL HARDOVER & OTHER WARNINGS
procedures.subtitle: Rotor brake, hardover/servojam, bleed valve, ICS, abnormal governing, servo transparency

right: Wait until the rotor is at a standstill before leaving. With wind, head into the wind and hold the cyclic slightly into the wind.
LAND IMMEDIATELY if possible; after landing hydraulic cut-off switch OFF and apply engine and rotor shutdown.
Set IAS 40–60 kt (74–111 km/h), sideslip if necessary; hydraulic cut-off switch OFF and apply the HYDR procedure; LAND AS SOON AS POSSIBLE.
At high airspeed up to 20 daN (45 lbf) pull on the collective, 7–12 daN (16–27 lbf) push left and 2–4 daN (4.5–9 lbf) push forward on the cyclic.

A flag on the FLI or 3-data page. If it does not clear at high power, maximum power is reduced (especially in the cold); if it does not reappear at low power, the engine may surge. Avoid abrupt power changes; GOV lights; land as soon as practicable.
ICS OFF; check COM 1 ON and adjust the volume. VHF and audio warnings remain available to the right-hand pilot only via COM 1. Abort hoisting if the ICS fails.

The FADEC governs Nf significantly lower than usual (an erroneous collective anticipator signal). NR/Nf may drop to 360 rpm before GOV lights. If NR/Nf fall below 375 rpm: check engine parameters and that NR and Nf are aligned; land as soon as practicable. Avoid hovering with a left crosswind; make a no-hover landing.
Self-correcting: reduce the severity of the maneuver, follow the aircraft's natural reaction, let the collective decrease naturally (avoid low pitch) and smoothly counter the right cyclic motion.
Avoid inhalation of extinguisher agent as much as possible (RFM Section 3.4).
Ventilate the cabin thoroughly to clear smoke and extinguishing agent before continuing operations.
Check affected systems and wiring as required; coordinate with maintenance before next flight.

procedures.title: TAIL ROTOR FAILURE – HANDLING AND LANDING

right: Recognize uncontrolled yaw (typically to the left) and differentiate between loss of thrust and loss of control.
LAND IMMEDIATELY. Reduce twist grip to IDLE and increase collective as required to cushion touch-down as per Section 3.3 §1.1.
Simultaneously reduce collective depending on available height, move cyclic forward to gain speed and maintain Vy or higher, adjusting collective to minimize sideslip (Section 3.3 §1.2).
Maintain Vy or higher and adjust collective to obtain minimum sideslip; LAND AS SOON AS POSSIBLE on a site suitable for autorotation (Section 3.3 §1.3).

On a suitable area, perform an autorotative landing according to the ENGINE FLAME-OUT autorotation procedure (Section 3.2): maintain about Vy in the descent, flare at roughly 70 ft (21 m), level at around 20-25 ft (6-8 m) and cushion the touchdown with collective. Over water, aim to ditch with IAS below 30 kt (56 km/h) and minimum rate of descent, and keep the twist grip at IDLE during the descent.

In case of pedal jamming/loss of control, avoid airspeeds below about 20 kt, especially near the ground. Set IAS around 70 kt (130 km/h) in level flight, use HYD TEST / ACCU TST as described in Section 3.3 §2 and carry out a shallow running landing with slight left sideslip.

procedures.title: AUTOROTATION LANDING TRAINING
procedures.subtitle: Twist-grip failure simulation — full touchdown or power recovery (SUP.6)

right: Train within gliding distance of a suitable running landing area. The twist grip can be turned back to FLIGHT quickly at any time and at any NR.
Collective — REDUCE power.
Twist grip — IDLE. TWT GRIP light on, gong sounds, engine at idle (Ng about 68 %).
Autorotation procedure — APPLY actions 1 to 10 of Section 3.2 §1 of the basic manual.
Collective — REDUCE to full low pitch.
Twist grip — FLIGHT. Rotor speed rises to its normal governed value.
APPLY actions 1 to 4 of the autorotation procedure (Section 3.2 §1) — then:
Check NR in the normal operating range, then twist grip — FLIGHT. Nf increases to its governed value.
Collective — CONTROL to keep NR in the normal operating range.
Cyclic — FLARE.

steps.left: Power recovery — 6–9 (at 20–25 ft / 6–8 m, constant attitude)
right: Collective gradually increase to reduce rate of descent and forward speed; cyclic slightly forward for the landing attitude; pedals cancel any sideslip; collective increase as necessary.
No significant Nf transient is expected when switching from IDLE to FLIGHT in autorotation (torque about 0 %), because no power is required from the engine.

procedures.title: HYDRAULIC FAILURE TRAINING
procedures.subtitle: Single hydraulic system — simulation with ACCU TST, then the completed procedure (SUP.7)

right: Trained instructor with recent experience; flight risk assessment beforehand. With hydraulics off: no hover or low-speed maneuvers, no bank above 30°. No passengers other than observers with training duties.

Avoid heavy weights (higher control loads). Train close to an airfield suitable for a running landing. On a go-around, abort the training and reset the hydraulic cut-off switch to ON — expect a significant drop in control loads.
Never activate [ACCU TST] when the hydraulic cut-off switch (RH collective grip) is OFF.
Activate [ACCU TST]. Check HYDR flashes with the gong and the ACCU TST light is on.
Bank below 30°, avoid abrupt maneuvers, set IAS between 40 and 60 KIAS (74–111 km/h).
Reset [ACCU TST] to OFF. Check the light is off and HYDR out within 3 s. If it is not reset, hydraulic assistance cannot be restored.

[ACCU TST] also removes all tail rotor control assistance, so yaw pedal loads rise at once — this is not part of a real hydraulic failure. The first step can be skipped at the instructor's discretion.
Check IAS between 40 and 60 KIAS. Keep bank below 30° and do not attempt hover or low-speed maneuvers; do not move the twist grip out of FLIGHT as loads increase.
Hydraulic cut-off switch (RH collective grip) — OFF. Check HYDR and gong; control loads increase.
Complete the hydraulic failure emergency procedure.
Hydraulic cut-off switch — ON before the next takeoff or hover; check HYDR out within 3 s. The instructor stays ready to restore assistance at any time by setting the switch to ON.

procedures.title: EMERGENCY FLOATATION GEAR
procedures.subtitle: Limits, arming, inflation and autorotation onto water (SUP.17)

right: For emergency landing on water only; takeoff after an emergency landing on water is prohibited. Not certified for ditching.

Minimum weight with OAT < 0 °C: 1480 kg (3263 lb). Max IAS with the gear stowed and armed or inflated: 135 kt (250 km/h) power on; 100 kt (185 km/h) with torque below 40 %. Maximum altitude for inflation: 6600 ft (2000 m). Below 400 ft (122 m) above water the gear must be armed.
[FLOAT ARM] ON — check FLOAT ARM lights 1 and 2 ON. Disarm: [FLOAT ARM] OFF, check lights 1 and 2 OFF.
Floats LOCKED in the lowered position, protective covers CHECKED, pressure in both cylinders CHECKED against the placard.

steps.left: Failure with FLOAT ARM set to arm
right: Inflation not possible (also with EMER SW OFF or battery at EMER SHED): continue flight within gliding distance of land. Inflation possible on both floats: continue flight.
After an engine failure or urgent need to alight on water, check rotor speed. [FLOAT ARM] — ON.
FLOAT ARM lights 1 and 2 — CHECK ON (at least one).
[FLOAT FIRE] under guard on the collective grip — PRESS. Recommended IAS below 80 kt (148 km/h); above 80 KIAS a decelerating pitch-down can occur.
Collective — REDUCE to keep NR in the normal range. IAS — Vy.
If relight is impossible or after tail rotor failure: engine starting selector OFF. Head equally between wind and wave direction on final.

At about 70 ft (21 m) flare; at 20–25 ft (6–8 m) gradually increase collective; cyclic forward slightly for 10° nose-up and under 10 kt (19 km/h) at touchdown; pedals cancel sideslip; collective cushions the touchdown.
Collective gradually to full down, rotor brake APPLY, evacuate once the rotor has stopped. Afloat, open the forward doors with the door jettison handles.

procedures.title: DUAL HYDRAULIC SYSTEM MALFUNCTIONS
procedures.subtitle: Yaw servo seizure, tail rotor control loss, HYD1 / HYD2, SERVO, LIMIT (SUP.23)

right: Do not exceed a load factor that lights LIMIT.

steps.left: Loss of tail rotor control — symptom
right: Jammed pedals or loss of pedal effectiveness. Below 20 kt (37 km/h) and near the ground a go-around may be impossible because of lost fin efficiency.
Cyclic and collective — ADJUST to set IAS 70 kt (130 km/h) in level flight.
Hydraulic cut-off switch — OFF. Then [ACCU TST] — ON (pre-MOD 07.471) or PRESS for 2 s (post-MOD 07.471); the load compensator depressurizes.

steps.left: Loss of tail rotor control — landing
right: On a suitable area make a shallow approach with a slight left sideslip and a running landing. The sideslip reduces as airspeed falls and collective is applied. A right-hand wind component makes it easier.

steps.left: Yaw servo slide-valve seizure — hover, no yaw movement
right: Hydraulic cut-off switch — OFF; LAND normally. The yaw load compensator assists with heavier pedal forces.

steps.left: Yaw servo slide-valve seizure — hover, yaw rotation
right: Hydraulic cut-off switch — OFF; control yaw, LAND normally.
Airspeed — REDUCE to 40–60 kt (74–111 km/h) in level flight, sideslip if necessary. Hydraulic cut-off switch — OFF. Normal approach and landing.

Loss of pressure on that circuit. Keep a more or less level attitude, avoid abrupt maneuvers, bank below 30°, IAS below 110 kt (204 km/h) or VNE if less. One remaining circuit allows continued safe flight and landing. Land as soon as practicable; normal approach and landing.
Tail rotor control hydraulic power is lost: do not press [ACCU TST] — it would discharge the yaw load compensator and right pedal loads may become significant. LIMIT may come on with HYD1.
Jamming of a distributor valve on the main servo unit. Land as soon as practicable.

Main servo unit maximum load reached. In high-speed cruise or steep maneuvers reduce power on the collective and reduce speed or load factor on the cyclic — CONTINUE FLIGHT. LIMIT may appear with HYD1 in a real hydraulic failure.

procedures.title: AFCS FAILURES (SFIM 85 T 31)
procedures.subtitle: Uncommanded inputs, gyro, hardover, trim, AC and total electrical failure (SUP.16)

right: Disengaged on the ground except for checks; do not engage before takeoff if the trim test is not satisfactory; minimum height for hands-off operation 400 ft (120 m).
Jerks not caused by turbulence: disengage the AFCS. If the anomaly disappears, re-engage channels one at a time; disengage the faulty channel and re-engage the others as required. Continue flight.
Apply the hydraulic failure procedure and disengage the AFCS.

steps.left: Vertical gyro, gyro horizon or monitoring unit failure
right: Pitch, roll and monitoring unit disengage automatically; HDG, ALT and A/S are inoperative, yaw remains. Cyclic and collective — HANDS ON. Continue flight.
Faulty channel disengages automatically. Controls — HANDS ON; power reduction may be needed to keep within limits. Continue flight.
Yaw channel and HDG disengage; pitch and roll remain. Pedals — FEET ON. Continue flight.

Faulty trim disengages; the cyclic may move toward the failure first. Controls — HANDS ON. Press trim release momentarily; [PITCH TRIM]/[ROLL TRIM] — PRESS/OFF for the faulty channel; re-engage the AFCS; re-trim with the cyclic trim release. Continue flight.
Cyclic stick seizure: press trim release; if it persists press [TRIM REL] and apply 10 kg (22 lb) on the affected channel to break the trim shear device. Continue flight.
AFCS disengages. Controls — HANDS ON; check [INV] ON, press it back on if needed. Continue flight.
AFCS disengages automatically and cannot be re-engaged.

procedures.title: SAND FILTER
procedures.subtitle: P2 valve use, checks and failures (SUP.14)

right: Heating and demisting OFF when P2 is ON. P2 OFF in visible moisture with OAT below 0 °C. Flight in falling snow is permitted with P2 OFF.

Engine air intake and sand filter — clean, with no foreign objects, ice or snow in or around the intake and no stagnant water at the drain hole. Ice or snow left there can be ingested and cause a sudden engine failure.
[SAND FILT] ON — P2 on the VEMD; then OFF — P2 off.
Heating and demisting OFF; [SAND FILT] ON — P2 appears on the VEMD.
The P2 air valve fails to open: avoid flying in a sandy atmosphere.
The P2 air valve fails to close: continue flight, observing the P2 bleed-air limitations.
[SAND FILT] OFF. The FADEC takes the filter into account automatically.

procedures.title: HOIST OPERATIONS AND EMERGENCIES
procedures.subtitle: Checks, hoisting, hoist failure and engine failure (SUP.18 / 19)
procedures.rfmReference: H125 / AS350 B3 (2B1) RFM SUP.18 / SUP.19

right: One pilot and one hoist operator. Landing with a load on the hoist cable is prohibited; a hand cable cutter must be within reach of the operator.
Maximum load on the cable: 136 kg (300 lb) (SUP.18) or 204 kg (450 lb) (SUP.19).

Air Equipment: never more than 6 consecutive hoisting operations plus one descent with maximum load and maximum reel-out. Breeze: wait 30 s after each operation; after 3 complete cycles a 40 min stop is recommended.

Cable protectors on the landing gear on and secured; jib and locking device checked; hoist and cable condition checked; ICS checked; operator control grip, safety belt, glove and manual cable cutter in place. Check the load keeps the lateral CG within limits. Run-up: [HOIST] ON, check UP and DOWN operation, then reset to OFF.

Operator: glove on the guiding hand, safety belt fastened and secured. Pilot: ICS operative, doors opened on order at 60 kt (111 km/h) IAS or less (SUP.18), heating and demisting OFF, power margin and parameters checked.

The hook must touch the ground before the cable is grasped, to discharge static electricity. If the hook hits the upper mechanical stop forcefully, abort the mission. Jib in hoisting position, [HOIST] ON.
Pull the cable into the aircraft by hand, cut it, or return to base with the cable slightly inclined at VNE 60 kt (111 km/h).

Stop hoisting (do not use the speed control), inspect the cable, set the load down at the nearest suitable site, raise the cable by hand and store it in the cabin, [HOIST] OFF. If manual raising is not possible, cut with the manual cable cutter.

Collective — REDUCE according to height. Load — RELEASE as soon as possible with the cable-shear pushbutton. Pedals — control yaw. Cyclic — forward for speed. Collective — INCREASE to cushion touchdown. Pilot moves away to the right; ground crew move to the left.
Complete the present hoisting operation or abort the mission.
Jib in ferrying position, [HOIST] OFF, close the doors as required (check VNE with doors open).

procedures.title: EXTERNAL LOAD OPERATIONS AND EMERGENCIES
procedures.subtitle: Cargo sling 750 kg and cargo swing 1400 kg (SUP.12 / 13)
procedures.rfmReference: H125 / AS350 B3 (2B1) RFM SUP.12 / SUP.13

right: Maximum load: 750 kg (1660 lb) sling; 1400 kg (3086 lb) swing. Maximum all-up weight with load: 2800 kg (6173 lb) or the OGE-hover maximum, whichever is lower. Maximum IAS: 80 kt (148 km/h). Non-human external cargo only.
Jettisonable loads lifted free of land or water only. No empty net or unballasted sling unless the operator's approved procedures allow it.
[SLING] ON; load indicator ZERO (swing: LD ON lit, [ZERO] then [TEST]); hook opens in both electrical and mechanical modes; retaining latch free and its return spring working.
Load HOOKED and SECURED. Collective — INCREASE very smoothly, keeping the aircraft vertically above the load. Dwell briefly with cables tight. Lift the load vertically.
Check the load indication (swing: LD ON). Adjust the takeoff path to an immediate forward climb attitude. Check all parameters.
Apply the autorotation procedure and RELEASE the load as soon as possible.

Collective — REDUCE according to height. Load — RELEASE as soon as possible. Pedals — control yaw. Cyclic — forward. Collective — INCREASE to cushion touchdown. During hooking the pilot moves away to the right; ground crew to the left.
Collective lever mechanical release — ACTUATE.

LD ON comes on or goes out untimely — in the hover, release the load electrically and check the light: no change, abort the mission; status change, continue. In cruise make a precautionary approach to the nearest helipad first.

Train with gradually increasing loads. Use the shortest cable for a compact load. Keep a trailing cable or net clear of the tail rotor. Use the correct load attachment ring. Wet weather: thick rubber gloves and a conductor between ground and hook.

procedures.title: BAMBI BUCKET
procedures.subtitle: Model 2732S — limits, release and emergency jettison (SUP.52)

right: Use needs approval of the operational authorities. Capacity 1225 litres. Installed on the external load hook (SUP.13.1 or 13.2).
Empty bucket: VNE 90 kt (167 km/h). Bucket full or partly filled: VNE 80 kt (148 km/h).

[SLING] on the console switches the installation on. Cyclic-grip pushbutton releases the contents; second cyclic-grip pushbutton electrically releases the whole load; trigger under the collective releases it mechanically.
Bucket correctly secured; the shackle manufacturer's plate and the ballast inside the bucket face forward.
Cannot dump with the cyclic-grip control: place the bucket, full or empty, on the ground as with a sling load; ground staff unhook it with the load release device.
For a helicopter problem: release the bucket with the sling electrical or mechanical release controls, ideally in a right-hand turn with a slight load factor.
